steps.content: A stove fire flickers inside the inn, its flames trembling in the biting wind—flaring bright, then fading—threatening to go out entirely.

Jichuan sits cross-legged on the cold brick floor, her palm pressed against the chest of an elderly woman before her. Strands of luminous white internal force are being ripped from her meridians, flowing through her fingertips into the old woman's body.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Cough...
A dull blade might as well be carving open her blocked meridians, again and again. Cold sweat streams down her temples, runs along her cheeks, and seeps into her collar.
Stifled groans and coughs fill the air around her. Still, she does not dare stop, not for a single moment.

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
steps.content: Miss Jiang... please, child, you must rest... This old bone's lived her share. Don't you go wasting yourself on me...

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Be at ease, ma'am. Just a little longer, and the pain will pass.
As she speaks, she grits her teeth and forces out more of her internal force.

This is already the eighth person Jichuan treats without rest, but still, countless wounded cry out in agony around her. Her body sways unsteadily, and when the metallic taste of blood rises in her throat, she forces it back down.

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
steps.content: You've done more than any soul could ask, Miss Jiang... If it weren't for you, we'd all be frozen stiff by now.

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
steps.content: Don't push yourselves further for us... Our lives were never ours to keep. It's the heavens' call, not yours.
Jichuan steadies her voice, keeping it calm and controlled.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I'm fine... Cough... Every person who survives gives the rest a little more hope to hold on.

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
steps.content: Someone like you—young, skilled, noble—you shouldn't be trapped here, waiting to die with hopeless souls like us!

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
steps.content: Go home, child. Your parents must be waiting by the door.
Clouded eyes brimming with tears, the old woman holds Jichuan's gaze with quiet resolve. She keeps her voice low, ensuring the others in the room cannot overhear.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: There's no noble or common here. I have parents waiting for me, and so do your families. Don't they hope just as much to see you safe and sound?

Jichuan forces herself to hold her head still, to keep her gaze from drifting toward that distant window glowing with warm lamplight, the light her parents leave burning, always waiting for her return.
But the old woman's words—go home—wrap around her like a tender spell.
Go home... Yes, she has a home now. A home with warm tea and hot meals, with a cherished friend and a beloved family. And here... here remains an endless frozen world and a crowd of strangers.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>If this truly is the afterlife, then why must I endure such purgatory all over again... If only...</color><i>
Her healing hands never stop moving, though her thoughts drift away to that warm little house, to the hot soup her mother has waiting for her.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>What if none of this was ever real...</color><i>
A cruel, coldly rational thought flashes through her mind: perhaps all this suffering is mere illusion, her efforts no more than grasping at shadows.
Yet a cry immediately yanks her back from that brief lapse.

steps.speaker: Female Disaster Victim A
steps.content: Miss Jiang! My baby... she's crying again, and I don't know why...
Jichuan's hands reach out before her mind catches up. She draws the child into her arms, gently patting her back.
The heat against her fingertips makes her heart clench.
The clamoring thoughts in her mind fall away like a receding tide, leaving only one behind.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>But what if... what if this is real? What if these people are all truly alive?</color><i>
//Black Screen

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Chuan'er? Slacking off here again, are we? Have you finished memorizing the medicinal herbs I assigned?

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Mm... soon.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Oh-ho! So you've snuck my roasted beans again!

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: You're so stingy, Dad... I'll buy you a new bag next time I go down the mountain.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Hmm? What's the matter? Why do you look so bothered reading a storybook?

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Well... the hero in the story had a falling out with a friend. But I think both of them have a point...

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: The hero has been through so much hardship in the martial world that he wants to retreat from it all. But his friend says he's just being a coward...

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: I feel bad for the hero, but I also don't think he should just hide in the mountains forever...

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Dad, do you think he should go into seclusion, or keep wandering the world with his sword?

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Hah... you've got me there, sweetheart. I can't make other people's choices for them.

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: What if it were you?

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: The latter, of course.

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Why?

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Hmm... how to put this so you'll understand...

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: Alright, take these beans on the plate. See this bowl with a hundred beans? If you shared them with ninety-nine other people, how many would each get?

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: If I share with ninety-nine people, everyone gets one bean, and I'd have one left for myself.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: What if you only shared with ten people?

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Then everyone would get ten beans!
Her father scooped up all the remaining beans from the plate and pressed them into young Jichuan's hands.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: But if you took these and hid yourself away, you could keep all a hundred beans just for yourself.
Young Jichuan watched the beans stacked in her palms, thoughtful. Then she returned them all to the plate, taking not a single bean for herself.

steps.speaker: Young Jichuan
steps.content: Then I won't take any, so I can share with a whole hundred people!
//Black Screen
//Back to the inn
The raging snowstorm lashes the inn's weathered door, each gust a volley of steel blades forged from ice. The wooden bolt groans and creaks under the strain, on the verge of giving way.
Within the inn, firelight shudders and flickers across anxious faces. Dozens of elders, women, and children huddle in the shadows, their silent worry fixed upon the girl standing before the flames.
Jichuan returns the infant, whose fever has now broken, to the mother's waiting arms. She lifts a hand to her own mouth and wipes the fresh blood from her lip. It is done. She has made her choice.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>True or false, what does it matter? So long as there is the faintest possibility that suffering may unfold, I am bound to stand before it. This is the path my parents set beneath my feet, and the vow I made with Mudling: to become true martial heroes.</color><i>
She approaches the precarious wooden door, pulling it open just a sliver.
The storm outside gathers strength. Loose tiles plummet from the inn's roof, their landing smothered by the thick, forgiving snow.
The room does not comprehend this sudden act. Bewildered gazes linger on Jichuan's back, searching for a reason that is not there.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: This storm has caged you long enough. To linger here awaiting its mercy is to surrender what little warmth remains. Now, I alone may hold the means to break this impasse.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: What I do now may be like casting a candle into a river, futile in the eyes of reason, reckless in the eyes of prudence. Yet Heaven and Earth granted each of you this singular breath, and every life is as precious as the finest jade, never carved twice.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Though unworthy, I will offer my own steps to melt the ice that bars your way. With this resolve, I go now to carve a sanctuary for those who cannot yet raise a hand to shield themselves.
With that, she gives the infant in the woman's arms one final, gentle stroke upon the cheek. She exits the inn and presses forward, alone, into the teeth of the raging storm.
//Outside in the snowstorm
Even having channeled her internal force as a preemptive shield, Jichuan reels the instant she sets foot outside. The vicious wind shows no mercy.

Illness and cold conspire now, a united front ripping through meridians and scraping against her organs. She forces her pace to slow, allowing the fragile architecture of her body a single breath to recover.
She presses on toward the town center, where the storm's fury only intensifies. Walls groan and waver on the brink of collapse, while snow discharges from the rooftops in muffled, percussive thuds.
She enters the eye, and immediately, a low, stifled groan escapes her. Blood beads and trails from the corner of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Ice worms at the viscera, fire ants along the sinew... I have grown rather familiar with this pain. It would seem Heaven's playwright has but one tired act, staged again and again.
She presses a hand to her chest, suppressing the ache. A light flick shakes the snow from her plum branch, and she aims it at the dark, oppressive sky.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I believe the soul endures beyond the flesh. I believe the wheel turns, that all beings are granted a new beginning, and that threads severed too soon may yet be knotted anew in another dawn.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: And yet this world answers with the same unyielding judgment, afflicting the innocent, harvesting hope before its fruit can sweeten, and spinning mortal sorrow into a circle without end.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: This bitter cycle of endless parting, of impossible reunion... Let it befall me alone.
Her words fade into silence as the plum branch sweeps through the air. Internal force surges with the motion, etching intricate runes into the space before her.
The runes scatter outward, a spiraling weave that expands to form an immense array, large enough to envelop the entire town.
From this pattern, a luminous white barrier surges upward. The wind and snow crash furiously against the light, yet find themselves unable to penetrate even an inch.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Ngh...! What a pity. I left in such haste... In the end, I never did taste my mother's rice cakes again... Cough!
The barrier shines so brilliantly, sheltering the entire town, yet it cuts Jichuan off from her paradise, from home.
From the shelter of the ruined walls, the townsfolk begin to emerge, one by one. They fix their wide, shocked eyes on the barrier before them.

steps.speaker: Male Disaster Victim A
steps.content: A plum branch draws the array, golden light shields every soul, and the storm can't get through... Th-this is straight out of the tales of martial heroes. It's the Plum Immortal Calming the Snow!

steps.speaker: Male Disaster Victim B
steps.content: But there ain't no immortals in this world... She's just a girl, barely more than a child. She shouldn't have to...

Jichuan offers no explanation, nor does she glance behind her. The hand that grips the plum branch trembles without cease. Her face is pale as paper now, each breath more labored than the last. She feels it acutely that her life force is bleeding away with every shred of internal force she spends.
Yet she cannot retreat, not even half a step. She cannot pause, not even for a moment.
Behind her stand countless fragile lives, the mortal world she is sworn to protect at any cost.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I did not imagine this solitary stand would weigh heavier than the clash for the codex upon the manor cliffs.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Perhaps it is because I knew, back then... that spring mountains awaited at my back, and trusted hands to catch me should I fall. Even had I failed at the final step, the flame would have remained to greet the dawn I longed to see.
Heaven and earth fade into white. There in the center of that vast, desolate snowscape, Jichuan's frail body sways on the verge of collapse.
She lifts her gaze toward the mist-veiled horizon and murmurs to herself.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I never found the moment to tell that person... Though I cherish the warmth of spring, the brilliance of living light... I have come to understand that winter's snow, for all its solitude, holds a quiet radiance all its own.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I'm told there is no snow in DisCity. Whatever ill wind gave rise to this storm... I hope only that the next snow to fall descends upon a joyous day, soft as cotton down, stirring only tender thoughts of homecoming and reunion.

Her hands grow so heavy around the plum branch that she can no longer lift them, not even a fraction. But she clenches her jaw. Her knuckles turn white, her fingertips tremble without end, and she does not let go.

steps.speaker: Male Disaster Victim A
steps.content: Miss Jiang! Please, you gotta stop! Don't go throwing your life away for folks like us!

steps.speaker: Male Disaster Victim B
steps.content: How could we ever repay a kindness like this? We ain't worthy of such a sacrifice...

The pleas behind her fade beyond hearing now. With the last shred of consciousness she still holds, she wears a peaceful smile. She will not let her parents and Mudling worry too much when they find her.
Her awareness fades further. She staggers, sways, and then her strength abandons her. She drops heavily to one knee, the plum branch plunging into the frozen earth with a sharp hiss.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: How wonderful... The snow... it seems lighter now.

Bit by bit, the light fades—from ashen gray to murky gloom—until only endless darkness remains. Jichuan seems to see that familiar window again, warm and glowing. Her parents and Mudling smile and wave, beckoning her home.
She tries to lift her hand to wave back, but her fingers are too heavy. The snow has risen past her waist unseen, crept over her chest, and now swallows her whole.
//Black screen for a while
BOOM!!
//White flash cuts to a ray of light
Just as the snow is about to swallow Jichuan completely, a thunderous roar tears through the heavens.
A bolt of lightning rips the pallid clouds apart, and golden radiance pours down from above, striking the small snowdrift that buries her.
A golden rift splits open within the beam of light. Through it, a pair of hands reaches out and grasps Jichuan's hand—still visible above the snow—with a firm, unyielding grip.
I'm sorry. I should have come sooner.

Your consciousness was a mess of blizzards and mountain trails. You know I'm terrible with that kind of weather and terrain. If you hadn't disguised yourself as Shuang'er to guide me, I wouldn't have even found the manor's entrance.
//Intense BGM plays, Chief's portrait appears, snowy landscape background

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So, what should I call you this time? The little beggar girl, the manor master, or...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Jichuan, the one who fought the cold eating away at her body until the very last moment inside her own consciousness.

Jichuan is pulled free. She stares at the figure before her, consciousness still hazy, still confused. She blinks and shakes her head hard. The figure does not vanish; it only sharpens, growing clearer by the moment.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Why are you here? What... is all of this?

You do not wait for her to finish. The shackles pierce through, linking palm to palm. The excruciating pain that wracks Jichuan's body begins to recede, and the haze that clouds her mind slowly sharpens into clarity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After you left the manor, I never stopped looking for you. Everyone in town was searching too... Do you remember Bao?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Of course... A girl just past twelve. Among all the children who came to hear my stories, she alone would linger behind and pester me with endless questions.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's the one who found you in that cave. She took good care of you, and when she heard I was searching, she did everything she could to reach me.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Bao found me... Then I am still alive?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're still alive. Do you remember Aunt Liu from town? Chen, the blacksmith? And that inn server who was always ducking under the tables?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I remember them all. After my parents passed, their friends from every corner of the land came to the manor of their own accord, to watch over me, to teach me. But I was a restless, wayward child. I had no patience for classical texts and formal instruction. I would slip down the mountain whenever I could and lose myself among the townspeople, under the name Shuang'er.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yeah, the townspeople all pitched in. They had Eastian merchant caravans send aged wheat all the way to DisCity, just so they could ask me to bring back their martial heroine of Northwild.
The snow keeps falling, but as Jichuan turns to look at the people behind her, their faces sharpen in the cold wind. One by one, they come into focus.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This isn't the afterlife. It's the final vision your mind created while fighting off death. It's everything you couldn't let go of, everything you couldn't escape from in those last moments. Your regrets, your attachments, your obsessions... All the deepest bonds of your life are here.
In disbelief, Jichuan touches the snow upon the ground and feels, to her surprise, a gentle warmth. A dazed, wondering smile crosses her face.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: No wonder I lost my way here... But what of you?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Is your presence here a true thread connecting to the waking world... or merely the projection of one I hold most dear?
Her question is so sincere that, for a moment, it leaves you without words.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well... Our brilliant manor master is a strategist of exceptional wisdom, isn't she? Once you wake and return to reality, I imagine you'll know the answer well enough.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So wake up. The rescue team will arrive soon to get you proper treatment. Spring hasn't come to Northwild yet. You promised you'd see it with me. Don't go breaking your word now.
You reach out your hand to her, but she only shakes her head in refusal.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Now that I understand the nature of this realm, no storm can lead me astray again. But I cannot leave with you just yet. There is something I must do first.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Do not worry. This time, I will not break my word. Wait for me outside.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Allow me to see you off first—

With a single thought, she drives the plum branch into the snow. It takes root in an instant. The shoots grow visibly, thickening and strengthening as flowering branches spread outward until the canopy covers the entire town, a shelter against every wind, every frost, every drop of rain and flake of snow.
The flowering canopy lifts you too, raising you toward the edge of this world. Through the dense tangle of plum branches, you see her serene smile receding into the distance.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your mind's fully stabilized now, but your body still isn't ready to wake completely. I'll find a way to deal with the Mania contamination.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I will leave that to you!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't mention it. Then it's settled. See you in reality.
//BG: Paradise Cottage
When Jichuan returns to that cottage, everything remains exactly as she left it. Within the flickering candlelight, three figures gaze out at her with tender eyes.
This is all she has left to do, to see them one last time. But Jichuan does not cross the threshold. She remains outside the cottage, standing still and quiet.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Mother
steps.content: Are you leaving now, my child?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Yes, it is time. I have made a promise to another, and many things are yet to be finished.

steps.speaker: Jichuan's Father
steps.content: The road ahead is long and winding. Walk with care, and guard your own well-being. That is what matters most to us.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I understand. Father, Mother... please take care as well.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Chuan! You better work twice as hard, once for you and once for me, and become the greatest hero this world's ever seen!

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: ...Pinky swear! On my honor, I shall become a hero worthy of the name, and wherever injustice darkens the land, my hand shall rise in your place!
//Black Screen
//BG: Cave
//Communicator rings

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I found Jichuan. Her mental state's stable. I've got the Mania contained, so it won't spread any further through her system. But physically, she's in rough shape. Still not out of the woods. We need to loop in Banyan Medical College for a joint consult.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Copy that, Chief. The rescue team has just linked up with our Eastian informant, Bao. They'll be arriving at your location shortly.
You watch the gradual steadying of Jichuan's breath and let out the sigh you have been holding.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've never been to DisCity, have you? Wake up soon. I'll show you around myself.
